title: Staggered release conductor for private control plane with tenant safety shields
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customers occasionally require control plane version promotions that need to be safe, auditable, and reversible. Current manual upgrade playbooks are slow and error-prone for large tenant populations. Goal: Implement a Staggered Release Conductor (SRC) that drives Terraform-based release waves with tenant-aware grouping, automated preflight simulations, and deterministic rollback. The conductor should be reusable across on-prem and VPC installs, produce audit logs for compliance, and integrate with Console telemetry for SLO-driven gating. This ticket covers design and the first implementation of the conductor's core orchestration + Terraform pipeline hooks.

Scope and out of scope:
- In scope: Terraform pipeline recipes, wave definition DSL, health gate evaluation engine connected to metrics/trace dashboards, tenant fractionation algorithm, automated rollback trigger and audit trail.
- Out of scope: UI for creating waves in Console (follow-up), operator-managed on-prem deployment packaging (follow-up).

Success criteria:
- SRC can run a multi-wave promotion against a staging pool and complete a successful rollforward in <30 minutes for a 2-wave demo run.
- Automated gates halt promotion if latency p50 or error rate breaches thresholds for >3 consecutive evaluation windows.
- Terraform plan/apply steps are produced as auditable artifacts and can be executed manually or by CI.
- Canaries include tenant isolation: customers in a wave are tagged and can be reverted without affecting other tenants.

Architectural notes:
- Conductor is implemented as a stateless controller that stores run state in a versioned S3 bucket (or equivalent object store) for private customers; state format will be JSON-lines and include diffs for change auditing.
- Waves are defined via a small DSL YAML that maps to Terraform workspace operations; the conductor will generate per-wave Terraform plans and a deterministic apply order.
- Health gates evaluate Console metrics via a read-only metrics API and a synthetic probe runner that can execute smoke requests through a tenant's VPC ingress.
- Rollback logic supports both automated fast fail (immediate revert of last wave) and staged rollback (segmented reverse waves).

Key constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Deterministic auditing vs. real-time speed: writing verbose change diffs increases artifact size but simplifies compliance reviews. We accept larger artifact size for first implementation.
- Using Terraform apply vs. API-driven changes: Terraform gives customers an auditable canonical artifact; we will implement Terraform-first and add API-mode later.
- Tenant fractionation: we choose algorithmic grouping by traffic profile + sibling-service affinity rather than pure random to minimize blast radius for dependent services.

Telemetry/metrics required:
- Per-wave latency p50/p95, error rate, request rate; synthetic probe success/failure; terraform plan/apply duration; audit log write latency.

Rollout plan (high level):
- Spike (week 1): prototype conductor generating per-wave Terraform plans and executing in a sandbox workspace.
- Integration (week 2): hook conductor to metrics API, implement gate evaluation and synthetic smoke runner.
- Canary demo (week 3): run a 2-wave promotion against staging tenants, collect telemetry, and test rollback paths.
- Harden (week 4): add audit packaging, increase test coverage, document operator runbook.

Terraform changes summary:
- New module private/controlplane-wave: parametric module that accepts target version, tenant list, and per-tenant overrides.
- Terraform pipeline adaptor: CI job templates that accept per-wave plan artifacts and can apply with a gated approval step.
- Workspace isolation: each wave uses a dedicated workspace to allow safe plan/apply and targeted rollback.

Health checks and gating rules:
- Gate window: 60s evaluation windows, 3 consecutive windows to trigger action.
- Thresholds (initial): latency p95 > 450ms OR error rate > 0.8% for gate fail. Thresholds will be tuned post-demo.
- Synthetic probe: 5 requests per window per canary tenant hitting a representative endpoint (inference ping + health).
- Probe fallback: if synthetic runner cannot reach tenant VPC, mark wave as BLOCKED and surface operator instruction for network debugging.

Dependencies:
- Console metrics read-only API (PM-req: metrics-filter-v2)
- Terraform module library updates in repo infra/terraform-modules (PR incoming)
- CI pipelines to support per-wave artifact staging (infra-team)

Attachments / Links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/private-deployments/src-conductor-design (placeholder)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9872
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/controlplane-upgrades

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the wave DSL (safety, expressiveness) and the audit schema.
- Security review required before GA for customers with compliance needs (FedRAMP/GxP).
acceptance_criteria: Conductor generates per-wave Terraform plans and uploads artifacts to object store
Integration tests simulate synthetic probes and can trigger automated rollback
Audit artifacts (plan diffs + execution log) are persisted and viewable
Demo 2-wave promotion completes with expected gate behavior and documented metrics
rollout_plan: Week 1: Prototype plan generation and S3 artifact storage
Week 2: Metrics integration and synthetic probe runner
Week 3: Canary demo against staging tenants; capture telemetry
Week 4: Harden, add runbook, security review
terraform_changes: Add module private/controlplane-wave with tenant scoping
Add CI adaptor that consumes per-wave plan artifacts
Workspace isolation per wave with naming convention: src-<run>-wave-<n>
health_checks: Console metrics gate evaluator (60s windows, 3 consecutive windows)
Network reachability check for tenant VPC ingress
Terraform plan/apply success and duration metrics
